Managing water scarcity begins long before water scarcity.
REKK's water resource management guide presents an approach that is also close to the AquaRE approach:
• You have to start from the local conditions. Different solutions work in areas with different water balances.
• Water requirements must also be addressed. Rationalising urban and economic water use is one of the means of preventing crises.
• Technology alone is not enough. In addition to investments, regulation, organization and cooperation between actors are also decisive.
• The possibilities of water retention are determined by the water balance of the landscape. Soil water reserves and land use are therefore key issues.

Mennyibe kerül valójában az aszály?
Az aszálykárokról gyakran mezőgazdasági problémaként beszélünk, pedig a hatás nem áll meg a földek szélén.
Az MNB 2026-ra már számszerűsítette ennek makrogazdasági következményeit:
• a mezőgazdaság hozzáadott értéke akár 15%-kal csökkenhet, nagyrészt az extrém nyári időjárás miatt;
• ez önmagában 0,4 százalékponttal csökkentheti a GDP növekedését;
• a kukoricatermés az előző öt év átlagánál 51%-kal, a repce 26%-kal, a búza közel 22%-kal lehet alacsonyabb.
Ez jól mutatja, miért félrevezető a vízhiány költségét pusztán a közvetlen agrárkárral azonosítani.

A vízkockázat gazdasági kockázat.

És ha már a tétlenség költségét mérjük, a következő kérdésnek annak kell lennie: mennyibe került volna ezt a veszteséget megelőzni vagy mérsékelni – és mely alkalmazkodási beruházások térültek volna meg?

Forrás: Telex: Durván lehúzza az aszály a magyar gazdaságot idén, az MNB már ki is számolta, mekkora lehet a mínusz
https://telex.hu/gazdasag/2026/09/25/mnb-inflacios-jelentes-mezogazdasag-termes-aszaly-szarazsag

COP31 starts today.
I attended COP15 in Copenhagen with Simone Cooper-Searle, PhD; since then, I haven't felt that returning as a researcher would be the most useful contribution I could make.
But I still believe we can change course.
The Guardian's question — are climate talks getting anywhere? — is worth asking. For me, hope comes from connecting research with decisions, investment and people's everyday needs.
Electrification features prominently at this year's COP. And there is a strong economic case for moving faster - this is the cost of inaction. Investing now comes at a cost, of course, but delaying action carries a higher economic price: mounting climate damage, continued exposure to fossil fuel price shocks, and lost opportunities for growth and jobs.

Our Cambridge Econometrics modelling for CISL's Powering Prosperity report suggests that an electrification-led UK pathway could deliver additional jobs while reducing dependence on imported fossil fuels. These are opportunities we can choose to pursue, anywhere.
We know enough to act, and much more becomes possible when we act together.

Are climate talks getting anywhere? What's the point? Ten years after the Paris treaty, are climate talks getting anywhere? | Cop31 | The Guardian https://bit.ly/4BXuXLE
Powering Prosperity: our modelling on electrification https://bit.ly/4sOYp1T

style_notes:
Open with one short line that states the point or asks the question (it is the hook).
Exact figures as • bullets, each tied to a named source.
Frame water and climate risk as economic risk; the cost of inaction is a recurring theme.
One short punch line on its own line.
Link back to AquaRE or my own experience in one line, never salesy.
End with a forward-looking question or a call to act together, then the source and link.
No hashtags, no emojis.
